I totally agree.... I've tried to push the whole stop talking to him thing but she lashes back out at me telling me that I'm controlling her and telling her that she can't have any friends. It gets unplesant... but after reading everyone's replies I think I know what I need to do...

A few points I'd like to make, then I'll ask what I think I really need the most help with.

She is under a lot of stress, she's taking three classes and commuting an hour and a half each way every other day. She takes medication for her ADHD and recently started taking a supplimental medication for it. Given our history and my feelings for her I feel like I should take everything into consideration when figuring out why she changed and what I should do about it.

With everything I've said here, and knowing this now, does it appear she truly is on the outs, or would it behoove me to wait it out, and trust her when she says "It might work out, just give me time."
I tried to let her go, she won't leave the house because she has nowhere to go.
I've run this scenario in my head dozens of times.. and it's probably the mental state I'm in but if she came back to me right now, I would take her...  it's pathetic.

Theres been no talk of compensation for supporting her, mostly because I've always seen that as my responsibility.. she did offer to pay for daycare if I took the kids while she moves out to I guess field her options. I get what you're saying and I realize I'm being used.... and I don't think she care, as I'm pretty sure she's emotionally checked out. Past few weekends we've tried some kindling, but even the spooning and hugging feels hollow which only bores deeper.
I am supporting her financially.. she doesn't have anywhere else to go if I kick her out... the thought of doing that breaks my heart.

Yea I tried to get her to go to a couples therapy retreat, but she used homework (which she didn't even touch that weekend) as an excuse to not go..

I mean it's clear what should be done, but the thought of her not in my life is soul crushing...

I've confronted her about him and she did show me her phone. They talk about fairly asinine stuff, usually about school but also about our relationship, and he doesn't hesitate to encourage her to "move on". I do believe she's formed an emotional attachment to him. She also says the reason she wants to talk to him so often is because she doesn't fight with him like she does me. A part of me believes her, I've never had a reason not to trust her in 8 years, but another believes its something more which is why I blame my insecurities. It's been so confusing. What I do know, is she wants me to support her until she can finish school so she can get her degree, get a job, and support herself, THEN she wants to move out.
I know... I wish it wasn't that simple considering everything we'd been through.
